title: ECB June 11 Rate Hike Fully Priced as Eurozone May Inflation Flash Estimate Due June 2
detail: Financial markets on May 31 are fully pricing a 25 basis point rate hike by the European Central Bank at its June 11 monetary policy meeting, which would lift the deposit facility rate from 2.00% to 2.25%. The hawkish pivot follows the confirmed surge in eurozone HICP inflation to 3.0% in April 2026 — driven by energy at +10.8% YoY — which itself was influenced by Middle East tensions and an earlier-than-expected rebound in energy prices. The May 2026 Eurostat flash inflation estimate is scheduled for release on June 2, and a reading above 3.0% would cement expectations of two consecutive hikes (June and September), potentially lifting the rate to 2.50% by end-Q3. ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane had noted in May that the bank 'cannot look through' the energy-driven inflation rebound as it risks feeding into wage negotiations across the eurozone.

title: AI Act Digital Omnibus: EP Formal Adoption Vote Scheduled June 14-17 — Simplified Compliance Regime Imminent
detail: The European Parliament is preparing for a formal plenary adoption vote on June 14-17 on the AI Act Digital Omnibus amendments — a simplification package agreed in political deal between the Council and Parliament on May 7, 2026. The Omnibus extends high-risk AI compliance deadlines under Annex III to December 2027 and Annex I to August 2028, introduces extended sandbox periods for SMEs, and adds a new categorical ban on AI-powered 'nudifier' applications effective December 2, 2026. Formal adoption before August 2, 2026 would ensure the amendments take effect before the AI Act's full enforcement date for general-purpose AI (GPAI) models. SMEs across the EU are welcoming the extended deadlines, while civil society organisations warned against weakening protections for workers subject to automated decision-making systems.

title: EU-Western Balkans Summit Preparations: Tivat, Montenegro Hosts June 5 Summit for First Time
detail: Final preparations are underway for the EU-Western Balkans Summit in Tivat, Montenegro on June 5, 2026 — the first time Montenegro has hosted this annual diplomatic gathering, coinciding with the country's 20th anniversary of independence. European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will attend alongside Western Balkans leaders. The summit agenda focuses on enlargement progress, particularly Montenegro's target of closing all negotiating chapters by end-2026 ahead of 2028 membership, the Growth Plan for the Western Balkans (€6 billion package), and status updates on Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania, Bosnia, and Kosovo. The Macron-Spajić meeting on May 27 was part of a wider diplomatic sprint in the week before the summit to consolidate political commitments. A ceremonial dinner on June 4 will mark Montenegro's independence anniversary with EU leaders.
